Hi team — a few technical notes and recommendations from infra: 

1) Connection & keep-alive: k6 default HTTP/1.1 connections work fine. For streaming we recommend using HTTP/1.1 chunked responses; if your runner supports HTTP/2 we can test that too but ensure your client reassembly logic handles partial frames.

2) Timeouts: set client-side read timeout to 90s for long-gen flows; server-side default is 120s. If you see read timeouts we can bump server-side for the test.

3) Concurrency profile: please include a mix — 60% short streaming sessions (avg 30s), 40% long-gen sessions (avg 120–180s). This helps us exercise KV cache and batching behavior.

4) Backpressure and throttling: if the soft per-key RPS cap hits 300 rps, our runtime returns 429 with Retry-After. Our k6 script includes retry/backoff logic; if you want to avoid 429s we can provision a temporary bump to 600 rps for the 4-hour window. Let me know which you'd prefer.

5) Observability: we will instrument spans for request path, kernel selection, and kv-cache hit-rate. After the run we will share token-level cost and latency breakdowns.

I'll be on standby during the test window to tweak timeouts and temporary caps.

-Rishi
